title: Index words by length with toMap, merging the words that collide

blocks.text: `Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)` builds a map from a stream, but it throws `IllegalStateException` the moment two elements produce the same key. The three-argument form takes a merge function for that case, and the four-argument form also takes the map to fill.

Write `LengthIndex.byLength(List<String> words)`. It returns a map from each word length to the words of that length, joined with `", "` in list order. The map's keys come in the order each length first appears in the list.
Mind the collisions, the order of the keys, and the order of the words inside one value.

cases.says: It maps each length to its word when no two words share a length.
Words of the same length are merged into one entry instead of throwing IllegalStateException.
The map lists lengths in the order they first appear, which a plain HashMap does not keep.
Merged words appear in list order: the earlier word comes first.
Two words of length 200 still share one entry: lengths are compared with equals, and == on boxed Integers only works for small values.

concepts: toMap throws IllegalStateException on a duplicate key unless it is given a merge function.
The four-argument toMap chooses the map, such as a LinkedHashMap that keeps first-seen order.
